title: First 48 Hours in Osaka on a Budget
creator: Hannah Reyes
description:
Two days, one tiny capsule hotel and way too much street food. Everything I spent is listed below.

Learning Japanese with Parlo, the sponsor of this video. Try Parlo free for a month: https://parlo.app/hannah

Budget breakdown:
Capsule hotel: 3,800 yen/night
Food: about 3,000 yen/day
Transport: ICOCA card

sentences.t: Good morning from Osaka, it is six thirty and I have not slept, but I am so happy.
My flight landed at Kansai last night, and I took the train in and checked into a capsule hotel in Namba.
It costs about thirty eight hundred yen a night, which is, like, twenty six dollars, and it's spotless.
The capsule is honestly cozier than I expected, there's a little light, a fan, and a shelf for my phone.
The only downside is the man three capsules down who snores like a motorbike.
Okay, breakfast.
I'm going to a convenience store, because Japanese convenience stores are a whole tourist attraction on their own.
I got an egg sandwich, a salmon onigiri, and a cold coffee, and the total was under six hundred yen.
This egg sandwich is unreasonably good, I don't know what they do to the eggs, but it's illegal somewhere.
After that I walked up to Osaka Castle, which takes about forty minutes from Namba if you go along the river.
The grounds are free, you only pay if you want to go inside the main tower, which I skipped to save money.
Then I tried to buy a train ticket back and completely froze at the machine because a lady asked me something and I just smiled and nodded.
Okay, real talk, how many of you have booked a trip somewhere and still don't know how to say thank you in the language?
Because that was me two months ago, which is why I started using Parlo, who are sponsoring this video.
Parlo is a language app built around real conversations, so instead of memorizing random words, you practice ordering food, asking for directions, and checking into a hotel.
It has a speaking mode that listens to your pronunciation and tells you where you're going wrong, which my Japanese desperately needed.
Ten minutes a day on the bus to work, and I could actually order my own ramen last night.
You can try Parlo free for a whole month at parlo.app/hannah, and the link is in the description.
So, after my little ticket machine crisis, I headed to Kuromon Market for lunch.
It's touristy and a little pricey, but you can graze if you're careful.
I had grilled scallops for five hundred yen and a single giant strawberry that cost way more than a strawberry should.
No regrets about the strawberry.
In the afternoon I took a nap in the capsule, which is the most budget travel sentence I've ever said.
Then at night, Dotonbori.
This is the famous street with the canal, the giant neon signs, and the running man sign everyone takes a photo with.
I did the takoyaki, obviously, octopus balls, eight for about six hundred yen.
Please let them cool down, I burned the roof of my mouth on the first one, every single person does.
Then okonomiyaki at a tiny place with six seats, where the guy cooks it right in front of you on the hot plate.
Day two, I went to Shinsekai, which is the older, kind of retro neighborhood with Tsutenkaku tower.
It's where you get kushikatsu, which is skewers of basically anything, battered and deep fried.
And there's one rule, you never double dip in the shared sauce.
There are actual signs on the wall about it.
So, my total for forty eight hours, not counting the flight, was about twenty one thousand yen including the hotel.
That's around a hundred and forty dollars for two very full days.
Tomorrow I'm taking the train to Nara to get bullied by deer, so stay tuned for that one.
Thank you so much for watching, bye!
